geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the monolithic bent-bar into a split-wing mass to create a clearer public threshold and reduce the sealed-object reading.
Introduce a wider central separation so the void becomes legible as usable shared space rather than decorative subtraction.
Keep the dominant split aligned to the long axis so the mass still reads as one coherent building gesture.
Make the new split-wing controller the root so the geometry compiler preserves the added public void as the primary spatial rule.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the primary mass as a courtyard-forming anchor rather than an abstract sealed object, so the dominant gesture can support an inhabitable public void.
Open a larger, more legible void to create usable public space and better respond to the mixed-use street condition.
Align the public void to the verified access side in the program frame so the frontage reads as a deliberate threshold.
Lower the terrace link so the ground response becomes more immediate and public instead of remaining mostly upper-level.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact dominant mass in all four views, so it has basic geometric coherence, but the form is overly pyramidal/fortress-like and the hierarchy is weakly expressed. The blue frontage edge is not answered by a convincing public threshold; the ground is largely sealed, with only a shallow or incidental notch/void. In plan and section, the mass behaves more like a faceted object than a neighborhood-living building with active street edge, clear public space, and calm upper massing. The silhouette is not inherently bad as a stepped or tapered section, but here the steps do not produce a legible inhabited terrace or usable court. Programmatically it feels closer to an abstract object or office/tower gesture than a mixed neighborhood building with active ground relation. Because the core semantic invariant of an active, legible street threshold is not met, program_fit_hard_pass fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than this neighborhood-living brief; copy the void logic, not the scale or vertical typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Tall prismatic massing with a carved, legible central void and a clear urban edge relationship; useful as a precedent for strong dominant mass plus subtraction.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Photographic courtyard atmosphere is not the same as massing clarity; use only the court/threshold principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/stepped composition around a sheltered outdoor court; helps reinforce active ground and inhabitable void.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more monolithic and less permeable; this reference suggests opening the ground more decisively.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise courtyard enclosure with porous edges and a protected interior public room.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Typology is too vertical and office-driven for this brief; only the ground-threshold relation transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Useful for understanding a mixed-use tower/ground split and a stronger base-to-top hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual to the brief: too infrastructural/pedestrian-object oriented and not a neighborhood building mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Bridge-like connection and linear public passage can inform access sequencing.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied, but containment alone is not sufficient.
The frontage edge remains semantically under-addressed; the blue access line does not receive a clear public void or entry seam.
The current silhouette is too monolithic and mass-object driven for the neighborhood-living brief.
Visible void is small and not clearly public or inhabitable.
Do not treat the stepped top as a successful program section unless it produces clear terrace/ground consequence.
